main_text.l: ris & Liberorum divortio proximus certe
(imo major in nonnullis) dolor, cùm ab his
plus forsan humanis affectibus indulgeatur[?] in
praesens, Illi in Gratiae Caelestis incrementum
profint.
Hoc Me solatur, quod his Mediis Ordin-
a-rius necessariò destitutos solet Deus Donis suis
& Gratiâ extraordinario quodam modo supplere.
Si Me Spiritus illius erudire & infirmitates
meas (quod spero) adjuvare voluerit orantis,
legentis, meditantis, haud jam alio Oratore
aut Doctore opus.

l.i: Ad Te igitur, Deus Meus, has jam Preces

main_text.l: meas solitarias dirigo: quod alienae opis deest per
immediatam tui Spiritus assistentiam supple, qui
& tenebras meas solum illustrare potest, & exci-
tare torporem.

l.i: O Tu Sol Iustitiae Sacer Fons Caelestis Lucis &
Ardoris, Clarifica cor meum & accende, docens
Me simul, & pro Me intercedens. In Te Omnis
Plenitudo, A Te Omnis abundantia; Per Te
Omnis acceptatio, Tu mihi in societatem, in sola-
tium sufficis. Tu Rex meus es, esto mihi & Pro-

main_text.l: pheta, & Sacerdos Regas Me, erudias Me,
pro Me precare, & mihi semper praesens sis.
Valuit olim in Te colluctatio Jacob in illo Sa-
cro duello, cùm nemo esset praeter Te qui assist-
eret. Tu Illum roborc[?] donasti quo Te vincere, &

l.i: grata quadam violentia benedictionem à Te

page.notes: Printed text at the very top-left edge is a fragment ("ris") that continues from the previous page. The page number reads "213" with a worn 3. The Greek running head is set in capitals; the letters were read from the scan and may differ slightly in the Σ/Ι forms. "indulgeatur" appears with a c-like e and is doubtful. "roborc" is a probable misprint for "robore" and is copied as printed. Italic and roman distinctions in the long paragraphs are approximate. The large initial "Ad" and "Valuit" are copied as plain letters. Bleed-through from the facing page and faint digitiser text at the bottom right were left out.
